definitions.explanation: Refers collectively to multiple newspapers, treating each as a separate source. Standard journalism vocabulary for 'the press' considered paper-by-paper.

examples.japanese: {各紙|かくし}が{報道|ほうどう}した。
examples.english: Each of the newspapers reported it.

examples.japanese: {事件|じけん}は{各紙|かくし}の{一面|いちめん}を{飾|かざ}った。
examples.english: The incident made the front page of every paper.

examples.japanese: {社説|しゃせつ}を{比|くら}べると、{各紙|かくし}の{立場|たちば}の{違|ちが}いがよくわかる。
examples.english: Comparing the editorials, you can clearly see the difference in each paper's stance.

notes:
A formal compound: {各|かく} (each) + {紙|し} (here meaning newspaper, an abbreviation of {新聞|しんぶん}). Appears mostly in news, commentary, and writing about media.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {各紙|かくし}が{報|ほう}じる: each paper reports
- {各紙|かくし}の{社説|しゃせつ}: editorials of the various papers
- {全国|ぜんこく}{各紙|かくし}: all the national papers

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {各社|かくしゃ}: each company — broader; covers any kind of company (TV networks, publishers, etc.)
- {新聞各社|しんぶんかくしゃ}: each newspaper company — refers to the publishers; {各紙|かくし} refers to the papers themselves
- マスコミ: mass media — much broader and informal
